items.title: One of the largest Swiss Chalet restaurants to be demolished for development in Mississauga
items.summary: A Mississauga residential development is slated to replace one of the largest Swiss Chalet restaurants in Canada. , a two-storey commercial plaza with a Swiss Chalet near Sherwood Village (previously Sheridan Centre). The development, which would include 142 back-to-back townhomes, a 10-storey apartment building with 241 units and a public park, was approved at the City of Mississauga’s Planning and Development Committee last week. , submitted to the city. Ward 2 Coun. Alvin Tedjo noted the Swiss Chalet is one of the largest in the country. “We are going to lose that, but that’s okay because I am sure there is lots of space across the street, over at Sherwood Village,” Tedjo said. Community members expressed concerns about the loss of the plaza and its businesses. Staff suggested that the nearby Sherwood Village mall is a main retail centre for the area. Sheridan Corporate Centre is a two-storey plaza at 2155 Leanne Blvd.

items.title: New campaign seeks to get people out to vote in Mississauga
items.summary: With voter turnout in Mississauga among the lowest in Ontario four years ago, a new community campaign is urging more people to get out to the polls in the 2026 municipal election. Voice the Vote in Mississauga, described by organizers as a non-partisan voting engagement campaign, is being lauched Monday night at Burnhamthorpe Community Centre. com. ” With election night set for Oct. 26, the four main mayoral candidates in Mississauga — incumbent Carolyn Parrish, former mayor Bonnie Crombie and city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla — officially kicked off their campaigns and opened up their respective headquarters over the weekend. In all, 14 candidates are running to become mayor of Canada’s seventh-largest city while 75 hopefuls, among them nine incumbents, are competing for city council seats to represent Mississauga’s 11 wards. 5 per cent in 2018). The 2022 voter turnout amounted to 107,310 ballots being cast, City of Mississauga figures show.

items.title: House of the week: Custom-built home in sought-after Mississauga neighbourhood
items.summary: This place: A custom-built home in a sought-after Mississauga neighbourhood. Features: This custom-built home in Mineola, offers over 4,600 square feet of living space. Upon entry, a double-height foyer sets the tone, leading into interiors finished with hardwood floors, large windows and designer lighting. There is a formal dining room, and the living room features a coffered ceiling, custom built-ins, integrated surround sound and a fireplace. The main-floor office has cathedral ceilings, built-in speakers and large windows. The kitchen showcases Cambria quartz countertops, premium GE appliances, custom cabinetry and a centre island connected to the main living areas. Sliding doors open to a covered porch. Upstairs, the primary bedroom features vaulted ceilings, a walk-in closet and an ensuite bathroom complete with a soaker tub, double vanities and a glass-enclosed shower. The additional bedrooms are filled with natural light, and each offer access to an ensuite or semi-ensuite bathroom. The finished basement features a recreation space with rough-ins for heated floors. Additional highlights include central vacuum, integrated surround sound, a hard-wired security system, custom built-ins and a double garage. The home is near schools, golf clubs, Port Credit, lakefront parks and major highways including the QEW, Highway 427 and Highway 401. Thanks to Sam McDadi Real Estate Inc. Brokerage for all the information about the House of the Week.

items.title: Shots fired twice at same lounge in Mississauga
items.summary: Shots were fired at the same Mississauga lounge twice in the last week. The shots were fired at the Sapphire Lounge at 168 Queen St. S. in Streetsville, reports indicate. m. on Sunday, Sept. com. There were no reported injuries as the business was closed at the time and no one was inside, the spokesperson said. There was a similar incident at the same location approximately one week ago, police said. A post on Reddit shows police tape at the lounge on Sept. 7. Police said the investigation is still active and ongoing. There was no further information on suspects.

items.title: DIANNE STELLA CHOPTIANY Obituary | Toronto Star
items.summary: CHOPTIANY, DIANNE STELLA January 7, 1950 - September 9, 2026 Dianne Stella Choptiany, passed away on September 9, 2026, in Mississauga Credit Valley Hospital, after a courageous 29-year battle with cancer. She was born on January 7, 1950, in Toronto, and lived a life marked by love, generosity, and quiet strength. She will be remembered always for the warmth she brought to others, the steadiness of her presence, and the many ways she made the lives of those around her brighter. Despite how she was feeling after chemo and other treatments, she always put on a brave face. ; her son, Ben Palka, and his wife, Teri, along with their daughters, Victoria and Alexandra; her daughter, Tammara Teeter, and her children, Brandon and Rhyan; and her son, Christopher Choptiany, and his partner, AJ, along with their daughters, Adalyne, Audryna, Aurora, and Autumn, born September 8, 2026. Dianne cherished each member of her family deeply, and her love for them was unwavering. She took great joy in being present for their milestones, celebrations, and everyday lives, and she leaves behind a legacy of devotion that will continue through them. m. m. Interment to follow at Springcreek Cemetery, 1390 Clarkson Rd. , Mississauga. In Dianne's memory, donations may be made to the Canadian Cancer Society or Princess Margaret Hospital. ca. items.title: A City in Tune returns to celebrate the music and musicians that helped shape Mississauga
items.summary: The Museums of Mississauga exhibit runs from September 24 to December 27, 2026. Entertainment and activities | September 14, 2026 Back for the second year, A City in Tune: Mississauga’s Greatest Hits, returns to Adamson Estate from September 24 to December 27, 2026. Presented by the Museums of Mississauga, the exhibit explores the people, places and sounds that have helped define Mississauga’s music story. This all-new exhibition invites visitors to listen, reflect and learn about Mississauga’s impressive and diverse musical talent. Explore artifacts, instruments and archival materials from artists such as Triumph, Donna Grantis and Billy Talent. See large-scale portraits of some of the city’s best-known musicians, check out a map of iconic music venues and attractions, and listen to curated playlists featuring artists connected to Mississauga. Join the Museums team on Saturday, September 26 for the opening reception. This is your opportunity to be among the first to explore the exhibit and celebrate the homegrown talent, memorable moments and local stories behind Mississauga’s music history. A City in Tune: Mississauga’s Greatest Hits exhibition Adamson Estate 850 Enola Ave. m.

The race for the top job at city hall is heating up in Mississauga as two high profile candidates launched their campaigns on Sunday, setting up a showdown between the city’s current and former mayor. Carolyn Parrish is Mississauga’s incumbent, and she’s looking to secure her first full term in next month’s municipal election after winning a byelection in 2024 when Bonnie Crombie stepped down in order to run for the leadership of the Ontario Liberal Party. However, after failing to win a seat in the provincial legislature, Crombie decided to return to municipal politics and try to win her old job back. During Sunday’s campaign kickoff, it was clear there is no love lost between the two rivals.

items.title: Compass Food Bank annual walk aims to raise $200,000 to help 2,000+ people weekly
items.summary: Check out the top trending stories across Ontario this week,… Highway 10, Highway 401, Highway 403, Highway 410, Highway 9… Participants at the 2025 annual walk event, which raised $178,000. The funds provided more than eight weeks of food and hygiene supplies for local students. The Compass Food Bank is organizing and hosting its 20th annual walk on Saturday, Sept. 19 in Mississauga. The event will take place at Church of St. Mark-Lutheran located at 130 Mineola Rd. E. m. to noon and will mark two decades of the organization’s community fundraising efforts, according to the food bank’s website. This year’s fundraising goal is $200,000. All proceeds will help provide food and hygiene items for individuals and families in south Mississauga who are experiencing food insecurity and are unhoused, according to the organizer. The initiative supports more than 2,000 individuals every week — one-third are children who rely on the service. The organization provides weekly access to food, according to the website. During the past 20 years, the walk has helped raise more than $750,000.
